title: FiveM stuck on "Loading add-on data files"
summary: The loading bar freezes while FiveM loads server content. Almost always a corrupted cache or antivirus blocking the files.
cause: FiveM downloads each server's content into a local cache. If a download was interrupted, or your antivirus scans and locks files while FiveM reads them, loading stalls.
steps: Close FiveM completely.
Open FiveM Application Data (right-click the FiveM shortcut > Open file location).
Inside 'data', delete the 'cache', 'server-cache' and 'server-cache-priv' folders. Leave 'game-storage' alone if you want to avoid re-downloading the base game files.
Add your FiveM folder to your antivirus exclusions (Bitdefender, Norton, and Avast are common culprits).
Relaunch and reconnect. The first load will be slower while the cache rebuilds.
ifStillBroken: Try a different server. If only one server hangs, the problem is likely on their end — report it to their staff.

title: FiveM crash: Window Watchdog / game hangs then closes
summary: FiveM's watchdog closed the game because it stopped responding. A frequent cause is antivirus software injecting into the game process.
cause: Some antivirus suites load their own DLLs into running programs to monitor them. FiveM treats the resulting stall as a hang and shuts down. The crash report often lists an antivirus DLL near the top.
steps: Open the crash report and look for DLL names from your antivirus (for example Bitdefender's 'atcuf' or 'bdhkm' modules).
Add exclusions for the FiveM folder and for the FiveM game process in your antivirus.
If your antivirus has an 'Advanced Threat Defense' or behavior-monitoring feature, add FiveM as an exception there too.
Close overlay tools that inject into games (old RivaTuner versions, screen recorders) and test again.
ifStillBroken: Temporarily disable the antivirus for one session to confirm. If the crash stops, it's the antivirus — keep the exclusions and contact their support.

title: FiveM: CURL error 18 when connecting
summary: A download from the server stopped partway through. Usually a corrupt cache file or a network hiccup.
cause: Error 18 means the connection closed before the whole file arrived. Bad cache entries, DNS problems, or a VPN can all trigger it.
steps: Clear the FiveM cache folders ('cache', 'server-cache', 'server-cache-priv').
Switch to a public DNS (for example 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8) in your network adapter settings.
Turn off any VPN or proxy and reconnect.
If you're on Wi-Fi, try a wired connection to rule out drops.
ifStillBroken: If it only happens on one server, their file host may be overloaded — try again later or tell their staff.

title: FiveM crash: CMoveAnimatedBuilding pool full
summary: This is a server problem, not your PC. The map has more animated objects (doors, gates, garage doors) than the game engine can track.
cause: GTA V has a hard limit on animated building objects. Servers with heavy custom maps (MLOs) can exceed it in busy areas, crashing anyone who gets close.
steps: Note where you were when it crashed (street, building, interior).
Send the crash report and location to the server's staff — only they can fix it by trimming map content.
As a workaround, avoid that area or approach it from a different direction so fewer objects load at once.
No changes to your graphics settings or files will fix this one.
ifStillBroken: If it happens everywhere on every server, it isn't this issue — paste your full crash log into the decoder on the home page.

title: FiveM crash pointing to a .ybn collision file
summary: A broken map collision file on the server crashes you near a specific location. Server-side issue.
cause: Collision (.ybn) files define what you can walk and drive on. If a server ships a corrupt one, every player loading that area can crash.
steps: Copy the .ybn file name and resource name from the crash report.
Send both to the server's staff so they can fix or remove that asset.
Clear your cache once in case your copy of the file was the corrupt one.
Avoid the area until it's patched.
ifStillBroken: If the crash continues after clearing cache and staff confirm the file is fine, paste the full log for a deeper look.
